rules.statement: When a Claude Code permission ask/deny rule guards a sensitive root folder, cover every common way a command names it (quoted forms, after `(`, `;`, `&` or `|`, `./` and `../` prefixes, the bare folder as a standalone argument, and backslash forms for PowerShell) without relying on how Claude Code splits commands or strips quotes, but don't add a broad `*/name/*` pattern that would also match ordinary source folders.
rules.why: Narrow patterns let a careless or prompt-injected agent read the folder without a prompt through forms like `cd secrets && cat key` or `cat "secrets/key"`, while an over-broad pattern would prompt on source folders such as `src/Secrets/`.
rules.check: In a change to `.claude/settings.json` permission rules for a sensitive path, list the command forms (quoted, separator-adjacent, relative-prefixed, standalone argument, PowerShell backslash) and confirm each has a matching rule, and that no pattern also matches source paths.

rules.statement: In a test that checks a configured list of rules or entries, assert the full expected set (every entry, or exact equality), not a subset.
rules.why: If the test requires only some entries, deleting one of the others still passes, so a regression goes unnoticed.
rules.check: Compare the test's required list with the entries the change adds to the configuration, and flag any entry that is missing from the assertion.

rules.statement: Don't ask for a dated CHANGELOG release section to be moved under `## [Unreleased]` when the repository dates the release section in the pull request that makes the release and its release workflow tags from the newest changelog section.
rules.why: In such repositories an entry left under `[Unreleased]` would not be tagged or released when the pull request merges.
rules.check: Before reporting, look at the release workflow (does it tag from the newest changelog section?) and at earlier releases (were their sections dated in the release pull request?).
